newsitem.title: CANADA: United Tri-Star maintains Solv-Ex link.
newsitem.headline: United Tri-Star maintains Solv-Ex link.

text.p: United Tri-Star Resources Ltd said on Monday it continued to hold its stake in a limited partnership with cash-strapped oil sands developer Solv-Ex Corp.

United Tri-Star, which has a 10 percent interest in the partnership which is attempting to extract oil and metals from Alberta's oil sands, also said it was current in all its financial obligations under the agreement.

Controversial Solv-Ex said earlier it could seek creditor protection under Chapter 11 bankruptcy procedures in the United States if necessary while it tried to restructure an overall plan of action for its Northern Alberta project.
The company said it filed a petition in Canada to stay actions by creditors against the project, for which the company had been seeking additional financing.
Additional financing for the project fell through after a drop in the company's share price, Solv-Ex Chairman John Randall said.
Solv-Ex said plant operations were reduced and security guards would be at the plant site near Fort McMurray, Alberta until new financing could be completed.
United Tri-Star said it also continued to hold 10-percent ownership of the oil sands lease and rights in the Solv-Ex technology outside the partnership.

Amid charges that its technology to extract oil and alumina from oil sands without the need for tailings ponds would not work, Solv-Ex's stock price and ability to secure financing has hampered the completion of its plant.
The Albuquerque, N.M.-based company has been the focus of numerous lawsuits and investigations into trading in its shares by short-sellers. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
